claims.text: The registry is mandated by ICD 906 D.9.b: CAPCO shall 'Manage a CAP Registry that maintains a list of all control systems, including all compartments and sub-compartments. ODNI CAPCO shall also ensure deconfliction or all other programs, and manage all compartment and sub compartment names, codenames, and any other pertinent information.'

A single ODNI office holds an authoritative, complete list of every IC compartment and sub-compartment codename, including unacknowledged ones, and is charged with deconflicting them against 'all other programs' -- which necessarily means CAPCO has visibility across the DoD/IC boundary. That register, not any congressional document, is the closest thing to a master index of the classified compartment space. Reasoning stated from D.9.b.

sources.name: IC Authorized Classification and Control Markings Register and Manual v5.1 (CAPCO)

desc: The CAPCO Register is the rulebook for how classified material is marked across the United States government, and reading it tells you how a special access program looks on paper. The publicly released Volume 5, Edition 1 (Version 5.1), effective 30 December 2011 with an administrative update of 30 March 2012, establishes a distinct Special Access Program Markings category - moved in that edition out of the Non-Intelligence Community Dissemination Control Markings category - which follows the SCI control markings in the banner line. 'The first value in the SAP category is the SAP category indicator either "SPECIAL ACCESS REQUIRED-" or "SAR-" (the authorized abbreviation) ... Following the SAP category indicator shall be the SAP program indicator which is the program's nickname or authorized digraph or trigraph.' Compartments follow the program identifier separated by hyphens; sub-compartments follow the compartment. That syntax is why the sample DoD action memo in DoDI 5205.11 is marked '(S//SAR-GTE)'. The Register was produced by CAPCO with the IC Classification Markings Implementation Working Group, whose members include the Air Force, Army, CIA, Coast Guard, DEA, DHS, DIA, DOE, State, FBI, Marine Corps, Navy, NGA, NRO, NSA, ODNI, OUSD(I) and Treasury, advised by NARA's Information Security Oversight Office. And the title page of the public version carries the note that settles a recurring argument: 'Certain security markings were removed due to classified content. These markings have been compiled in separate classified addenda.' The public register is therefore known, on its own face, to be incomplete - there exist compartment markings whose very existence is classified, listed in addenda that have never been released.
